resultJson.description:
Reviewer discovery tiers mirroring flow discovery (ADR 0021 §5): project `{workDir}/.orca/reviewers/*.md`, global `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/orca/reviewers/*.md`, built-in resources. Precedence project > global > built-in by filename stem; a discovered reviewer with a shipped name replaces it in place (documented override mechanism); additive reviewers join both presets. Prerequisite refactor: the review loop and selector read description/file pattern from the reviewer definition itself, deleting the parallel by-name maps so there is one source of truth. Discovery happens once per run at context construction (like stack settings) and is exposed on `FlowContext`; `allReviewers`/`minimalReviewers` gain `(using FlowContext)`. New ADR 0023. Orca's own project reviewer committed at `.orca/reviewers/orca.md`.

Report verification notes: the parallel maps are consumed by `ReviewerSelector.agentDriven`, not the loop, and are already derived from `ReviewerPrompts.all`; the real duplication is the by-name join between a `List[Agent[?]]` roster and the maps, which a custom/discovered reviewer falls through. `.orca/reviewers/` is collision-free. Shipped prompt files carry a `name:` frontmatter key the loader ignores — identity is the filename stem, and discovered files follow the same rule.

tasks.title: Carry reviewer metadata into the roster: ReviewerAgent and RosterEntry
tasks.description: In `flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/Reviewers.scala` add `final case class ReviewerAgent[B <: BackendTag](definition: Reviewer, agent: Agent[B])` (scaladoc: a reviewer ready to run — its definition, which the selector reads, and the read-only agent built for it). Change `buildReviewers` to return `List[ReviewerAgent[B]]` (still `withSystemPrompt/withName(r.name)/withReadOnly`), and `allReviewers`/`minimalReviewers` accordingly. In `ReviewerRoster.scala` make `RosterEntry` wrap a `ReviewerAgent[?]` plus `ReviewerId`, exposing public `name` (= definition.name), `description`, `filePattern: Option[Regex]`, and `private[review] agent`; `RosterEntry.roster(reviewers: List[ReviewerAgent[?]])`. In `ReviewLoop.scala` change `reviewAndFixLoop`, `reviewThenFix` and `ReviewLoopConfig` to take `reviewers: List[ReviewerAgent[?]]`. Leave `ReviewerSelector` and the `ReviewerPrompts` maps untouched in this task (next task consumes the new fields). Update `runner/src/main/scala/orca/exports.scala` (export `ReviewerAgent`), `flows/review.sc` (`Par.mapUnordered` over `ReviewerAgent`s: `r.agent.resultAs[...]`, name from `r.definition.name`), `FlowCompilesTest` (`val _: List[ReviewerAgent[?]] = buildReviewers(claude, list)` and the other pins), README review-utilities table text where it says `buildReviewers` returns agents. Tests: add a helper in `ReviewLoopFixture` that wraps a fake agent into a `ReviewerAgent` with a `Reviewer(name = agent.name, description = ..., systemPrompt = "")` and migrate `ReviewAndFixTest`/`ReviewChangeSetTest`/`ReviewerSelectorTest`/`AllReviewersTest` call sites; add one test that `RosterEntry.description`/`filePattern` reflect the definition. `sbt compile` warning-free, `sbt test` green, `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: Selector reads description and file pattern from the roster; delete the by-name maps
tasks.description: In `flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/ReviewerSelector.scala` drop the `descriptions` and `filePatterns` parameters of `agentDriven(agent, instructions, ...)`; build `ReviewerInfo(e.name, e.description)` from each `RosterEntry`; change `eligibleForPicker(all, changedFiles)` to use `e.filePattern` (same semantics: empty `changedFiles` keeps everyone and emits the Step naming file-gated entries; otherwise `filePattern.forall(rx => changedFiles.exists(rx.findFirstIn(_).isDefined))`); remove the all-empty-descriptions warning. Delete `ReviewerPrompts.descriptionsBySlug` and `filePatternsBySlug` and every reference: `Reviewers.scala` scaladocs (Reviewer, ReviewerPrompts), `flows/review.sc` `pickReviewers` (filter with `r.filePattern`), `FlowCompilesTest` pins, README (selector table row `agentDriven(agent, instructions?)`, the `files:` paragraph, "Where the defaults live"). Update `ReviewerSelectorTest`: entries carry their own `filePattern`/description via the fixture helper; add one test that the picker is shown the description from the definition of a non-shipped reviewer (the case that previously reached the picker as a bare name). Keep the CC file compiling (pure `->` arrow unchanged). `sbt compile` warning-free, `sbt test`, `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: ReviewerCatalog: tiered discovery of reviewer .md files (pure, unwired)
tasks.description: 1) `tools/src/main/scala/orca/util/PromptResource.scala`: extract `parseWithMetadata(raw: String): ParsedPrompt` from `loadWithMetadata` (which becomes `parseWithMetadata(load(path))`); widen `ParsedPrompt` to `private[orca]`. 2) `tools/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaDir.scala`: add `reviewersPath(workDir) = root(workDir) / "reviewers"` (scaladoc: project-tier reviewer prompts, committed). 3) `flow/src/main/scala/orca/settings/GlobalSettings.scala`: add `reviewersPath(env, home)` = configHome/orca/reviewers and `defaultReviewers`; one test in `GlobalSettingsTest` mirroring the `flowsPath` one. 4) New `flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/ReviewerCatalog.scala`: `enum ReviewerOrigin { Project, Global, BuiltIn }` with a `label` extension ("project"/"global"/"built-in"); `case class DiscoveredReviewer(reviewer: Reviewer, origin: ReviewerOrigin, shadows: List[ReviewerOrigin])`; `case class ReviewerCatalog(all: List[Reviewer], minimal: List[Reviewer], discovered: List[DiscoveredReviewer])` where `discovered` lists only file-tier entries (winner first, shadows recorded) and a `describe: Option[String]` (or similar) that renders the one-line Step text, `None` when nothing was discovered; companion `builtIn: ReviewerCatalog` (shipped `all`/`minimal`, no discovered) and `discover(projectDir: os.Path, globalDir: os.Path): ReviewerCatalog`. Per tier: `*.md` regular files only (skip `os.isLink`), missing dir -> empty; slug = filename stem; parse with `PromptResource.parseWithMetadata`; missing `description:` or a `files:` value that fails `.r` -> `OrcaFlowException` naming the file and the key to fix. Resolution: project > global > built-in by slug; `all` = shipped order with shadowed slugs replaced in place, then additive slugs sorted by name; `minimal` = shipped minimal names through the same override plus all additive. Move `ReviewerPrompts.load` onto the shared frontmatter->Reviewer conversion so the shipped and file paths share one function. Tests in `flow/src/test/scala/orca/review/ReviewerCatalogTest.scala` over `TempDirs`: additive project reviewer appears in `all` and `minimal`; project shadows built-in `scala-fp` in place with `shadows = List(BuiltIn)`; project shadows global (both recorded); global-only reviewer; missing dirs tolerated; non-.md ignored; symlinked file skipped; missing description aborts naming the file; bad `files:` regex aborts; `builtIn.all == ReviewerPrompts.all`. Not wired into the run yet. `sbt compile` warning-free, `sbt test`, `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: Wire discovery into the run: FlowContext.reviewerCatalog, presets take FlowContext, setup Step
tasks.description: 1) `flow/src/main/scala/orca/FlowContext.scala`: add `def reviewerCatalog: ReviewerCatalog` (scaladoc: resolved once at run start from the three tiers, frozen; what `allReviewers`/`minimalReviewers` build from). `accessors.scala`: add `def reviewerCatalog(using ctx: FlowContext): ReviewerCatalog`. `TestFlowContext`/`TestFlowControl` (+ `TestFlowControl.create`) gain `reviewerCatalog: ReviewerCatalog = ReviewerCatalog.builtIn`. Any other `FlowContext` implementations (grep `extends FlowContext`/`FlowControl`) get the field. 2) `Reviewers.scala`: `allReviewers[B](base: Agent[B])(using ctx: FlowContext)` = `buildReviewers(base, ctx.reviewerCatalog.all)`; `minimalReviewers` likewise; scaladocs say the discovered tiers are included and that a same-named project/global file replaces the shipped reviewer. 3) `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala`: `flow(...)`/`runFlow` gain `globalReviewersPath: os.Path = GlobalSettings.defaultReviewers` (doc as for `globalSettingsPath`: tests override it, never read the developer's real config); in `buildContext`, inside the `surfaced` block after `readSettings` and before `FlowLifecycle.setup`, call `OrcaDir.assertNoOrcaSymlinks(workDir, OrcaDir.reviewersPath(workDir))` then `ReviewerCatalog.discover(OrcaDir.reviewersPath(workDir), globalReviewersPath)`; emit its Step text when present; pass the catalog into `DefaultFlowContext` as a constructor `val reviewerCatalog`. Update `RoleSettingsFlowTest` call sites that pass `globalSettingsPath` to also pass a temp `globalReviewersPath`. 4) `flows/review.sc`: pick from `reviewerCatalog.all` instead of `ReviewerPrompts.all` (comment only if file-specific). Built-in flows keep `allReviewers(reviewAgent)` unchanged — verify they still compile via `FlowCompilesTest` (add a pin that `allReviewers(claude)` resolves inside a stage and that `reviewerCatalog.all` is reachable from `import orca.*`). 5) Tests: a runner-level test (pattern: `RoleSettingsFlowTest`) that a `.orca/reviewers/x.md` in a temp repo shows up in `ctx.reviewerCatalog.all` and the setup Step names it; one that a malformed file aborts before setup (no branch created). 6) README: in "Settings" add the reviewer tiers (paths, precedence, override-by-name, frontmatter keys, identity = filename stem, abort on malformed file); update the `allReviewers`/`minimalReviewers` rows and the "swap or extend" paragraph to mention the catalog. `sbt compile` warning-free, `sbt test`, `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: ADR 0023 reviewer discovery; amend ADR 0011/0019; AGENTS.md pointer
tasks.description: Write `adr/0023-reviewer-discovery.md` in the repo's ADR style (Context / Decision / Consequences, concise): the problem (project-only rules; shipped prompts go everywhere); the three tiers with paths (`{workDir}/.orca/reviewers/*.md`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/orca/reviewers/*.md`, built-in resources), precedence project > global > built-in by filename stem, shadowing as the documented way to override a shipped reviewer, additive reviewers joining both presets (why `minimal` includes them), the frontmatter contract (`description:` required, `files:` optional, `name:` ignored, body per ADR 0011), abort-before-mutation on a malformed file, symlink guard consistent with ADR 0019, the setup Step, no cap (the picker narrows), the single-source-of-truth change (`ReviewerAgent`/`RosterEntry` carry description and file pattern; the by-name maps and `agentDriven`'s `descriptions`/`filePatterns` parameters are gone), and what is out of scope (shell listing/editing of reviewers). Add a dated amendment to ADR 0011 pointing at 0023 for discovery and the metadata change, and to ADR 0019's `.orca/` layout block adding `reviewers/` (committed). In AGENTS.md, under the `.orca` conventions, one sentence that project-specific review rules live in `.orca/reviewers/*.md` and are discovered per ADR 0023. Verify every path and symbol named in the ADR exists in the code (grep) before finishing; no code changes in this task.

tasks.title: Commit Orca's own project reviewer at .orca/reviewers/orca.md
tasks.description: Create `.orca/reviewers/orca.md` following ADR 0011's prompt conventions (frontmatter + short body, ~25 lines, `## Aspects` bullets, closing negative-scope line). Frontmatter: `description:` one or two sentences stating it enforces orca's own repository rules from AGENTS.md (with an "Include when:" hint: any Scala/flow-script change in this repository); `files: \.(scala|sc)$`. Aspects, each one line, distilled from AGENTS.md review-derived rules and project memory: (1) interfaces and persisted documents name git concepts, never a forge; forge-specific types stay in the package that talks to that forge; (2) new mutable state (`var` field, mutable collection, `AtomicReference`) is a design finding — the PR must state the alternatives rejected; Actor-held state and test helpers are the sanctioned exceptions; (3) no back-compat machinery and no default values on domain/persisted fields (the two documented exceptions: ProgressLog/SessionRecord tolerant decoding, RunManifest additive changes); (4) comments are present-tense facts: no history ("no longer", "renamed from"), no plan/epic labels, no teaching Scala mechanics; in `flows/*.sc` only file-specific facts; (5) capability discipline: `InStage.unsafe`/`WorkspaceWrite.unsafe` only inside `RuntimeInStage` and tests, never drop a `(using InStage)`/`(using WorkspaceWrite)` to make code compile, `WorkspaceWrite` never crosses a fork; (6) every write under `.orca/` goes through `OrcaDir.ensureRoot`/`ensureCache`; prefer `os.write` over `os.write.over`; (7) subprocesses capture stderr (`QuietProc.call` or a `CliRunner`); (8) domain modes are enums, never booleans or raw strings; three-plus same-typed adjacent params get named args or a case class; a wire field's absence is decided once at decode; one decision, one home; (9) user-facing refusals name the next action; destructive automatic operations state their purpose; (10) threat model: agents are trusted-but-fallible — do not report findings whose only justification is a malicious agent; (11) `.orca/settings.properties` is committed on purpose — never flag it. Closing line: do not re-report generic FP style, structure, naming, performance or test quality — those belong to the shipped reviewers. Verify the file loads: add a test in `flow` (or runner) that `ReviewerCatalog.discover` over this repository's `.orca/reviewers` (path relative to the sbt working dir, guarded to skip if absent) yields a reviewer named `orca` with a non-empty description and the `files:` pattern matching `Foo.scala` and `flows/x.sc` but not `README.md`. Keep the prompt short; no examples, no templated output format.

resultJson.brief:
## Build & conventions
- Scala 3 / Ox / sbt. Modules: `tools` (PromptResource, OrcaDir), `flow` (orca.review, FlowContext, settings), `runner` (flow() entry, DefaultFlowContext, FlowLifecycle, exports.scala, FlowCompilesTest), `shell`. Dependency order tools -> flow -> runner -> shell.
- Load the `direct-style-scala` skill before writing Scala (CLAUDE.md). Read AGENTS.md conventions: braceless, explicit return types on public members, no class-level `var`/mutable collections/`AtomicReference` (adding any is a design question — avoid it; everything here is pure data resolved once), enums not booleans, `OrcaFlowException` for user-facing aborts naming the next action, comments state present-tense facts (no history, no plan labels), 0.x so no back-compat shims, tests target one scenario each.
- Commands: `sbt compile` (must be warning-free: -Wunused:all, -Wvalue-discard, -Wnonunit-statement), `sbt test`, `sbt scalafmtAll` before finishing. Prefer plain `sbt` over `sbt --client` (AGENTS.md). Unit tests use munit, temp dirs via `orca.testkit.TempDirs.dir()`, `TestFlowContext`/`TestFlowControl` (flow/src/test/scala/orca/TestFlowContext.scala), `FakeAgent`/`StubAgent` fakes.
- Never commit unless the flow does it for you; never force-push.

## Current code (verified)
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/Reviewers.scala`: `case class Reviewer(name, description, systemPrompt, filePattern: Option[Regex] = None)`; `object ReviewerPrompts` with `Role`, private `load(slug)` reading `/orca/review/prompts/reviewers/$slug.md` via `PromptResource.loadWithMetadata` (`description:` required else RuntimeException; `files:` -> Regex), the 8 vals, `all`, `minimal` (CodeFunctionality, Readability, Test), `descriptionsBySlug`, `filePatternsBySlug`; top-level `allReviewers[B](base: Agent[B]): List[Agent[B]]`, `minimalReviewers`, `buildReviewers[B](base, reviewers: List[Reviewer]): List[Agent[B]]` = `base.withSystemPrompt(r.systemPrompt).withName(r.name).withReadOnly`.
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/ReviewerRoster.scala`: `private[review] opaque type ReviewerId = Int`; `final class RosterEntry private[review] (private[review] val agent: Agent[?], private[review] val id: ReviewerId)` with `def name = agent.name`; `RosterEntry.roster(agents: List[Agent[?]])`; `ReviewBatch`.
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/ReviewerSelector.scala` (compiled under captureChecking; `prepare` returns pure `->` arrow): `agentDriven(agent, instructions = ReviewLoopPrompts.SelectReviewers, descriptions = ReviewerPrompts.descriptionsBySlug, filePatterns = ReviewerPrompts.filePatternsBySlug)`; builds `ReviewerInfo(name, descriptions.getOrElse(name, ""))` (ReviewerInfo/ReviewerSelectionRequest live in `ReviewerSelectionRequest.scala`, non-CC); emits a Step when all descriptions empty; `eligibleForPicker(all, filePatterns, changedFiles)` keeps everyone when changedFiles is empty (emits Step naming file-gated ones) else filters by `filePatterns.get(e.name)`.
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/ReviewLoop.scala`: `reviewAndFixLoop[B](coderSession, reviewers: List[Agent[?]], task, ...)(using ctx: FlowContext, ev: InStage, fc: FlowControl, ws: WorkspaceWrite)`; `reviewThenFix` same; `private[review] case class ReviewLoopConfig(reviewers: List[Agent[?]], ...)`; `ReviewFixLoop` does `private val roster = RosterEntry.roster(reviewers)` and uses `e.agent` for turns (`e.agent.withRole(ReviewerPrompts.Role).chat()` ~line 704).
- Tests touching the roster/agents: `flow/src/test/scala/orca/review/{ReviewerSelectorTest,AllReviewersTest,ReviewAndFixTest,ReviewChangeSetTest,ReviewLoopFixture}.scala` (loop tests pass `reviewers = List(fakeAgent)` ~25 times; ReviewerSelectorTest builds `new RosterEntry(new FakeAgent("scala-fp"), ReviewerId(0))` and passes `filePatterns = Map(...)`); `runner/src/test/scala/flowtests/FlowCompilesTest.scala` pins the public surface (`val _: List[Agent[?]] = buildReviewers(claude, list)`, `descriptionsBySlug`, `filePatternsBySlug`, `allReviewers(codex)`).
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/exports.scala` re-exports `orca.review.{allReviewers, buildReviewers, minimalReviewers, Reviewer, ReviewerPrompts, RosterEntry, ...}` — add any new public type there.
- Flows: `flows/{simple,implement,implement-enhanced,implement-interactive,issue-pr,issue-pr-bugfix}.sc` call `allReviewers(reviewAgent)` inside a `stage`; `flows/review.sc` builds its own picker over `ReviewerPrompts.all`, uses `ReviewerPrompts.filePatternsBySlug` and runs `buildReviewers(...)` agents directly with `Par.mapUnordered(4)(agents): a => a.resultAs[ReviewResult]...` keyed by `a.name`. Flow comments must pass the locality test (only file-specific facts; no platform exposition).
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/FlowContext.scala`: trait with `workDir: os.Path`, `stackSettings: StackSettings` ("resolved once during lifecycle setup and frozen for the run" — the precedent to mirror), role agents, git/gh/fs, emit. `flow/src/main/scala/orca/accessors.scala` has top-level `reviewAgent(using ctx: FlowContext)` etc. Inside a `stage`, a `FlowControl <: FlowContext` given is in scope and wins implicit search for `FlowContext` — accessors already work there.
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/DefaultFlowContext.scala`: constructor takes `workDir`, role agents, tools, `stackSettings`, `startingCommit` as plain facts. `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala`: `flow(...)` -> `runFlow(..., globalSettingsPath: os.Path = GlobalSettings.default, ...)` -> `buildContext(...)` which inside `surfaced { }` calls `FlowLifecycle.readSettings(workDir, globalSettingsPath, stackSettings)` then `RoleAgents.resolveAll`, then `FlowLifecycle.setup` (tree mutation), then constructs `DefaultFlowContext`. Tests overriding the global path: `runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/RoleSettingsFlowTest.scala` (passes `globalSettingsPath = globalPath`).
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/settings/GlobalSettings.scala` (`private[orca]`): `configHome(env, home)`, `path`, `default`, `flowsPath(env, home)` = configHome/orca/flows, `defaultFlows`. Tests: `flow/src/test/scala/orca/settings/GlobalSettingsTest.scala`.
- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaDir.scala` (`private[orca]`): `root(workDir)`, `flowsPath(workDir)` = `.orca/flows`, `ensureFlows`, `assertNoOrcaSymlinks(workDir, dir)` (read-side guard; no-op when `.orca` missing), `abortIfOrcaComponentSymlink`.
- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/util/PromptResource.scala` (`private[orca]`): `load(path)` classpath only; `loadWithMetadata(path): ParsedPrompt` does the frontmatter split inline (`ParsedPrompt(metadata: Map[String,String], body)` is `private[util]`); `parseFrontmatterLine`, `unescapeYamlDoubleQuoted`.
- `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/flows/FlowCatalog.scala` (`private[shell]`, the model): `FlowOrigin {Project, Global, BuiltIn}` + `originLabel`; `DiscoveredFlow(name, description, origin, path, shadows: List[FlowOrigin])`; `list(projectFlows, globalFlows, builtIns)` groups per tier via `scriptsByName` (skips `os.isLink`, non-files, wrong extension; missing dir -> empty), resolves per name with winner first and `shadows = hits.tail`. Tests: `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/flows/FlowCatalogTest.scala`. The flow module cannot depend on shell, so write a sibling catalog in `orca.review`; mirror the shape, do not generalise.
- Shipped reviewer prompt format (ADR 0011): frontmatter `name:` (ignored), `description:` (required), optional `files:` (regex, substring-matched via `findFirstIn`); body ~25 lines: scope line, `## Aspects` bullets, negative-scope closing line. Only `scala-fp.md` declares `files: \.scala$`.
- Docs to keep in sync: README.md "Settings" section (~line 402) and the review utilities table (~line 699-797: `allReviewers`, `minimalReviewers` rows, selector table, the `agentDriven(agent, instructions?, descriptions?, filePatterns?)` row, "To swap or extend the reviewer set" paragraph, "Where the defaults live" list); AGENTS.md (review-derived rules ~line 288-325, `.orca` write rule ~line 372); ADR 0011 (roster + amendments), ADR 0019 (`.orca/` layout), ADR 0021 §5 (flow tiers). `.orca/settings.properties` is committed on purpose.

## Design decisions (settled — do not re-litigate)
- Single source of truth: metadata travels with the reviewer. New `final case class ReviewerAgent[B <: BackendTag](definition: Reviewer, agent: Agent[B])` in Reviewers.scala; `buildReviewers` returns `List[ReviewerAgent[B]]`; loop entry points take `List[ReviewerAgent[?]]`; `RosterEntry` wraps a `ReviewerAgent` and exposes `name` (= definition.name), `description`, `filePattern`, `agent`. Selector reads those; `descriptions`/`filePatterns` params and `ReviewerPrompts.descriptionsBySlug`/`filePatternsBySlug` are deleted; the all-empty-descriptions warning goes (description is a required field of `Reviewer`).
- Discovery result type `ReviewerCatalog(all: List[Reviewer], minimal: List[Reviewer], entries: List[DiscoveredReviewer])` where `DiscoveredReviewer(reviewer, origin: ReviewerOrigin, shadows: List[ReviewerOrigin])`; `ReviewerCatalog.builtIn` = shipped only; `ReviewerCatalog.discover(projectDir, globalDir)`. `all` keeps the shipped order with shadowed entries replaced in place, then additive discovered reviewers sorted by name. `minimal` = shipped minimal names resolved through the same override, plus every additive discovered reviewer (a project rule applies to small diffs too; the picker narrows).
- Identity is the filename stem (`orca.md` -> `orca`), same as shipped. A `name:` key is ignored.
- Errors in a discovered file (missing `description:`, invalid `files:` regex, unreadable) abort the run with `OrcaFlowException` naming the file and what to fix, before any tree mutation (inside `buildContext`'s `surfaced`, before `FlowLifecycle.setup`). Symlinked `.md` files are skipped; the project tier is guarded with `OrcaDir.assertNoOrcaSymlinks(workDir, OrcaDir.reviewersPath(workDir))` before reading.
- Exposure: `FlowContext.reviewerCatalog: ReviewerCatalog` (frozen per run like `stackSettings`), accessor `reviewerCatalog(using FlowContext)` in accessors.scala; `allReviewers[B](base)(using FlowContext)` = `buildReviewers(base, ctx.reviewerCatalog.all)`, `minimalReviewers` likewise. Setup emits one `OrcaEvent.Step` when anything was discovered, naming each discovered reviewer, its tier, and any shadowed tiers (e.g. `reviewers: orca (project); scala-fp (project, shadows built-in)`).
- Global tier path: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/orca/reviewers/` via `GlobalSettings.reviewersPath/defaultReviewers`; `runFlow` gains `globalReviewersPath: os.Path = GlobalSettings.defaultReviewers` beside `globalSettingsPath`, tests that override one override both with temp paths.
- No cap on discovered reviewers (picker narrows). No shell UI for listing reviewers in this epic.
- New ADR `adr/0023-reviewer-discovery.md`; ADR 0011 gets a short pointer amendment.

Its second half is a refactor of `globalSettingsPath`, which predates this change and has the identical exposure (a `flow()`-based test already reads the real `~/.config/orca/settings.properties`, and a malformed one already aborts it), so the reviewer tier adds no new class of exposure. Merging the pair and sweeping ~20 call sites belongs in its own change, where the settings half gets the same treatment.

issues.title: `ReviewerPromptFailure`'s structure is never read — only its message
issues.reason: An earlier round of this same review explicitly asked for the typed enum in place of thrown/stringly errors, citing substring-matching as the defect. Reversing it now would churn the same code twice in one change, and the enum grows to six cases and two construction sites with the accumulation fix.

issues.title: Two enums for one three-valued tier label
issues.reason: An earlier round of this same review asked for exactly this split, so `DiscoveredReviewer.tier` cannot be `BuiltIn` (make invalid states unrepresentable). Merging them back undoes an accepted fix from the previous round.

issues.title: `ReviewerOrigin` is a second copy of `FlowOrigin`, including the user-facing label strings the ADR requires to stay identical
issues.reason: A narrower re-report of a finding already declined on the epic's settled decision ("write a sibling catalog in orca.review; mirror the shape, do not generalise"). The extraction also rewrites `private[shell]` code — `FlowOrigin`, `originLabel` and its shell call sites — that this change does not otherwise touch. Worth doing as its own change.

issues.title: The project reviewer is far longer than the "short and concise list" asked for, and duplicates AGENTS.md by hand
issues.reason: Conflicts with I1.1 in this same round, which asks to add a twelfth rule, and with the task spec that enumerated the aspects item by item. The previous round's accepted fix deliberately kept the threat-model and settings.properties one-liners here while also recording them in AGENTS.md; I3.3 (fixed) addresses the mirror-scope half of this finding.

## Build & conventions
- Scala 3 / Ox / sbt. Modules: `tools` (PromptResource, OrcaDir), `flow` (orca.review, FlowContext, settings), `runner` (flow() entry, DefaultFlowContext, FlowLifecycle, exports.scala, FlowCompilesTest), `shell`. Dependency order tools -> flow -> runner -> shell.
- Load the `direct-style-scala` skill before writing Scala (CLAUDE.md). Read AGENTS.md conventions: braceless, explicit return types on public members, no class-level `var`/mutable collections/`AtomicReference` (adding any is a design question — avoid it; everything here is pure data resolved once), enums not booleans, `OrcaFlowException` for user-facing aborts naming the next action, comments state present-tense facts (no history, no plan labels), 0.x so no back-compat shims, tests target one scenario each.
- Commands: `sbt compile` (must be warning-free: -Wunused:all, -Wvalue-discard, -Wnonunit-statement), `sbt test`, `sbt scalafmtAll` before finishing. Prefer plain `sbt` over `sbt --client` (AGENTS.md). Unit tests use munit, temp dirs via `orca.testkit.TempDirs.dir()`, `TestFlowContext`/`TestFlowControl` (flow/src/test/scala/orca/TestFlowContext.scala), `FakeAgent`/`StubAgent` fakes.
- Never commit unless the flow does it for you; never force-push.

## Design decisions (settled — do not re-litigate)
- Single source of truth: metadata travels with the reviewer. New `final case class ReviewerAgent[B <: BackendTag](definition: Reviewer, agent: Agent[B])` in Reviewers.scala; `buildReviewers` returns `List[ReviewerAgent[B]]`; loop entry points take `List[ReviewerAgent[?]]`; `RosterEntry` wraps a `ReviewerAgent` and exposes `name` (= definition.name), `description`, `filePattern`, `agent`. Selector reads those; `descriptions`/`filePatterns` params and `ReviewerPrompts.descriptionsBySlug`/`filePatternsBySlug` are deleted; the all-empty-descriptions warning goes (description is a required field of `Reviewer`).
- Discovery result type `ReviewerCatalog(all: List[Reviewer], minimal: List[Reviewer], entries: List[DiscoveredReviewer])` where `DiscoveredReviewer(reviewer, origin: ReviewerOrigin, shadows: List[ReviewerOrigin])`; `ReviewerCatalog.builtIn` = shipped only; `ReviewerCatalog.discover(projectDir, globalDir)`. `all` keeps the shipped order with shadowed entries replaced in place, then additive discovered reviewers sorted by name. `minimal` = shipped minimal names resolved through the same override, plus every additive discovered reviewer (a project rule applies to small diffs too; the picker narrows).
- Identity is the filename stem (`orca.md` -> `orca`), same as shipped. A `name:` key is ignored.
- Errors in a discovered file (missing `description:`, invalid `files:` regex, unreadable) abort the run with `OrcaFlowException` naming the file and what to fix, before any tree mutation (inside `buildContext`'s `surfaced`, before `FlowLifecycle.setup`). Symlinked `.md` files are skipped; the project tier is guarded with `OrcaDir.assertNoOrcaSymlinks(workDir, OrcaDir.reviewersPath(workDir))` before reading.
- Exposure: `FlowContext.reviewerCatalog: ReviewerCatalog` (frozen per run like `stackSettings`), accessor `reviewerCatalog(using FlowContext)` in accessors.scala; `allReviewers[B](base)(using FlowContext)` = `buildReviewers(base, ctx.reviewerCatalog.all)`, `minimalReviewers` likewise. Setup emits one `OrcaEvent.Step` when anything was discovered, naming each discovered reviewer, its tier, and any shadowed tiers (e.g. `reviewers: orca (project); scala-fp (project, shadows built-in)`).
- Global tier path: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/orca/reviewers/` via `GlobalSettings.reviewersPath/defaultReviewers`; `runFlow` gains `globalReviewersPath: os.Path = GlobalSettings.defaultReviewers` beside `globalSettingsPath`, tests that override one override both with temp paths.
- No cap on discovered reviewers (picker narrows). No shell UI for listing reviewers in this epic.
- New ADR `adr/0023-reviewer-discovery.md`; ADR 0011 gets a short pointer amendment.
